beats.text: How much farmland does it take to feed one person? Guess the size.
All the farmland on Earth, split evenly between eight point two billion people.
Lock in your answer. Three. Two. One.
It's about fifty-nine hundred square meters. Almost a whole football pitch.
Eighty percent of it feeds animals: pasture and feed crops.
But that part gives us only seventeen percent of our calories.
Most of the field feeds animals. The small corner feeds most of us.

sources: Our World in Data, 'Half of the world's habitable land is used for agriculture' (Ritchie & Roser, updated 16 Feb 2024; data UN FAO and Poore & Nemecek 2018): agricultural land about 48 million km2; about 80% used for livestock (grazing plus cropland for feed), 16% crops for direct human food, 4% non-food crops; animal products supply about 17% of global calories and 38% of protein.
Per person: 48,000,000 km2 / 8.2 billion = about 5,850 m2 (world population mid-2026 about 8.2 billion, U.S. Census Bureau). Football pitch 105 m x 68 m = 7,140 m2 -> about 82%.
Global averages; actual land use per person varies a lot by country and diet.
